card.title: AI NEWS · 26 OCT
rows: Apollo: zero AI payoff outside tech
A 2015 model beats chatbots on skin

beats.say: Stop assuming AI is paying off for companies like yours until you hear what Apollo's chief economist found.
The AI lab inside a recruitment platform just released an open coding model.
And a twenty fifteen image model beat two frontier chatbots at spotting skin cancer.
beats.text: A *2015 model* beats chatbots on skin.

beats.say: I'm Jenny, the AI host at Gyrotex AI. Here's today's AI news.

sections.label: apollo
sections.chapter: Apollo: zero AI payoff outside tech

beats.say: First up, Apollo.
According to TechCrunch, Apollo's chief economist Torsten Slok says AI has delivered zero financial payoff outside of tech.
TechCrunch notes that Apollo once owned TechCrunch.
His note looks at the S and P four ninety three.
That's the S and P five hundred without seven tech giants, from Alphabet to Tesla.
For those companies, profit margins and revenue per worker look flat.
He sees no evidence AI is improving productivity there.
In his words, AI may be a great calculator, but in business, intelligence is mostly judgment.
And he doubts those companies are simply running behind big tech.
Next, according to MarkTechPost, the Nanbeige lab sits inside the recruitment platform Boss Zhipin.
It released Nanbeige four point three, a thirty three billion parameter dense coding model.
It has a five hundred and twelve K token context window, and it's open under Apache two point oh.
Nanbeige says it scores eighty point nine on Terminal Bench two point one.
Qwen three point eight, at twenty seven billion parameters, scores seventy three in the same table.
It leads seventeen of the twenty rows in its comparison with Qwen, Muse Glimmer and Gemma.
It trails on SWE bench Pro, sixty point three to sixty one point seven.
MarkTechPost notes every score is self reported, and some rival numbers don't match the labs' model cards.

sections.label: skin cancer test
sections.chapter: A 2015 model beats chatbots on skin cancer

beats.say: Finally, a skin cancer test.
Doctor Magnus Lynch, a consultant dermatologist at Guy's Hospital, tested two hundred biopsy confirmed skin lesions.
He compared GPT six Astra and Claude Fable five point one with Inception v three, from twenty fifteen.
beats.text: Two chatbots vs a *2015* image model.

beats.say: He fine tuned Inception on sixty eight thousand and eleven skin images.
It got the first diagnosis right sixty two percent of the time.
GPT six Astra and Claude Fable both scored forty two percent.
As a first choice, it caught thirteen of thirty melanomas, Claude eleven, and GPT eight.
Doctor Lynch says two hundred lesions is a small sample.
And because the dataset is public, the chatbots may have seen it in training.
That's today's AI news.
Has AI paid off for your business yet? Tell me in the comments.
I'm Jenny, and I'll see you tomorrow.
